sections.vendors: Next published its Corporate Responsibility Report to January 2026, disclosing that 627 processing sites have been onboarded to its traceability programme (300 of which are core), covering 84% of product volume. NEXT Sourcing Limited (NSL) continues to provide the primary buying and sourcing operations hub for Next own-brand.
sections.sustainability: Next has achieved 82% of main raw materials sourced through responsible or certified routes, tracking towards its 2030 target of 100%. Chemical management compliance stands at 84% of core textile wet processors engaged with the ZDHC Foundation. Next sources across Turkey, India, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka.
sections.sourcing: Next's responsible sourcing strategy focuses on traceability, raw material certification, nature and biodiversity, water and chemical management, and circularity. The brand is increasing disclosure of Tier 2 processing sites and targeting full coverage of Tier 1 and Tier 2 by 2028.
sections.strategy: Next continues to deliver strong financial performance as a platform business, with total platform sales (including third-party brands) growing faster than own-label. The brand's multi-channel strategy (stores + online + Total Platform) is generating competitive advantage in the mid-market.
sections.pricing: Next maintains its mid-market premium pricing position. The brand's ability to absorb sustainable material cost premiums through its strong margin profile is a strategic advantage over pure-value competitors.
sections.launches: Next's AW2026 own-brand range featured expanded Reiss and LABEL/ capsule lines alongside mainline. The brand continues to grow its premium private label range, including sustainable material lines under its responsible sourcing framework.
sections.gossip: Next Group's ownership of Reiss (since 2021 majority stake) means Reiss suppliers are increasingly integrated into Next's sourcing infrastructure. Some industry observers note this creates a two-speed supplier approval process — Next scale vs Reiss premium positioning.
soWhat: 84% responsible raw materials means approximately 16% of Next's sourcing is still through conventional routes — certified suppliers (BCI, GOTS, GRS, RWS) have clear headroom to win that remaining volume

627 processors tracked with 84% volume coverage signals that Next is close to full supply chain visibility — Tier 2 and Tier 3 suppliers who are not yet digitally traceable should urgently engage with Next's supplier platform

NSL's scale means Next is a high-volume, systems-driven buyer — suppliers who can integrate with Next's digital sourcing tools and provide real-time capacity and compliance data will have a competitive advantage
